Good morning, Claire. I am the Commercial Manager for the South and Southeast of Brazil, and I am based in Sao Paulo.
Good. And the people? I do not need the headcount of the whole country, only yours.
Seven direct reports, all of them in the field. I oversee the two regions and I report to the Commercial Director here in Brazil.
And what do you actually decide? Where does your scope stop?
I decide how we cover the territory and which accounts we protect. Pricing is outside my scope. We sell botulinum toxin, and our stakeholders are the doctors who prescribe it.
Thank you for saying that in plain words. Half this call has no idea what we sell in your market. One last thing: what are you changing this year?
At the moment we are rolling out a new coverage plan for the largest accounts. It is cross-functional — medical and marketing are in it with us.
That is the first introduction today that I will remember. Send me one page on the coverage plan and put me on the next review.

At the moment we are rolling out a new coverage plan.
Let me say that again, more slowly.

I meet a new country manager almost every month, and I always ask the same first question. Not how many people work for you. What do you actually decide? Because a job title tells me nothing. In one company a manager signs off on pricing, and in another company the same title cannot approve a lunch. So when someone introduces themselves to me and gives me only a title and a headcount, I still know nothing about them. Here is what I want, and it takes about forty seconds. Tell me the scope of the job. Tell me who reports to you and who you report to. Then tell me the one thing you are working on right now that will still matter in a year. That is it. And please do not apologise for your English before you start. I am not a native speaker either. Half of this company is not. Nobody has ever remembered an accent. Everybody remembers a manager who could not say what they were responsible for.

The first time I had to introduce myself in English to the global team, I prepared the wrong thing. I wrote a list. Fourteen items, everything I do in a week, and I read all of it. Nobody asked a single question at the end, and I thought it went well. It did not. A colleague told me afterwards that a list is the easiest thing in the world to forget. What people remember is a shape. So the second time I said three sentences. This is what my area covers. These are the people in it. This is what we are changing this year. Twenty five seconds instead of four minutes, and suddenly people started sending me emails about the thing we were changing. One more piece of advice, and it is the one I wish somebody had given me earlier. Say the name of your market out loud, early, in plain words. Most of the room has no idea what your business actually sells.

Good morning, everyone. My name is Renato and I am the Commercial Manager for the South and Southeast of Brazil. I oversee a team of seven consultants, and I report to the Commercial Director here in Sao Paulo. At the moment we are rolling out a new coverage plan for our largest accounts.
